probability_semantics: Native Human/AI/AI-edited/Humanized classes; not word shares or verified writing history.
cautions: In the saved 36-document English pilot, high-score false positives occurred on human writing. Do not treat a near-1 score as established authorship.
English four-class outputs are uncalibrated experimental auxiliary scores.

windows.quote:
For eight weeks, I read a chapter in the morning before looking at my phone, expecting to remember more of what I read. By the end, I could recall the plots of three novels. But I hadn't tested my memory before the experiment, so I can't tell whether my recall improved.

What changed was simpler: I stopped interrupting a chapter to check messages. I liked that. I still checked my phone as soon as I finished. I didn't keep to the routine every morning: on two mornings, I skipped reading altogether.

The reading itself was worthwhile to me even without evidence of a memory benefit. I'm reluctant to recommend the routine to everyone, though. My mornings were quiet during those weeks, and I didn't try it while travelling. Next month I want to try reading after dinner instead, although I haven't chosen a start date.

occlusion.interpretation: Sensitivity to deleting a paragraph. Positive delta means removal lowered the score; length/context changes confound this. This is not causal authorship evidence or a sentence probability.
